lines.en: Hi, Noah! Are you going to go to the mountains this weekend?
lines.pt: Oi, Noah! Você vai para as montanhas neste fim de semana?

lines.en: Yes! We’re going to drive to Gatlinburg. The mountains are more beautiful than the hills near Nashville.
lines.pt: Vou! Vamos de carro até Gatlinburg. As montanhas são mais bonitas que as colinas perto de Nashville.

lines.en: Are you going to stay in a hotel?
No, we’re going to stay in a cabin. It’s cheaper than a hotel.
lines.pt: Não, vamos ficar numa cabana. É mais barata que um hotel.

lines.en: Nice. Is the road longer than the road to the lake?
lines.pt: Legal. A estrada é mais longa que a do lago?

lines.en: Yes, the drive is longer, but the view is better.
lines.pt: É, a viagem é mais longa, mas a vista é melhor.

lines.en: What are you going to do there?
lines.pt: O que vocês vão fazer lá?

lines.en: We’re going to hike on Saturday. The trail is shorter than the one near my home.
lines.pt: Vamos fazer uma trilha no sábado. A trilha é mais curta que a perto da minha casa.

lines.en: You should take warm clothes. It’s colder in the mountains.
lines.pt: Você deve levar roupas quentes. Faz mais frio nas montanhas.

lines.en: Good idea. I’m going to bring a jacket and a hat.
lines.pt: Boa ideia. Vou levar uma jaqueta e um chapéu.

lines.en: Have fun! I’m going to visit the mountains in summer.
lines.pt: Divirta-se! Vou visitar as montanhas no verão.

facts.label: Planos e comparações
facts.sub: Use am/is/are going to + verbo para planos e -er than ou more + adjetivo para comparar: The cabin is cheaper than a hotel.

facts.label: Planos
facts.sub: Para falar de planos, use am/is/are going to + verbo base: We’re going to drive to the mountains. Para perguntar, use Are you going to…?

facts.label: Comparativos
facts.sub: Com adjetivos curtos, use -er + than: bigger than, cheaper than, longer than. Com adjetivos longos, use more: more beautiful than. Good vira better.

pages.title: A music shop · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Thursday evening in a music shop in Nashville. Guitars hang on the wall. Dean sits near the door with a small map. His friend Noah comes in with a big bag. The bag looks full of warm clothes. Dean asks about the weekend.

“Hi, Noah! Are you going to go to the mountains this weekend?” says Dean. “Yes! We’re going to drive to Gatlinburg. The mountains are more beautiful than the hills near Nashville.” says Noah. “Are you going to stay in a hotel?” says Dean.
